content.text: Meaning of excursion in English excursionnoun [ C ] us Your browser doesn't support HTML5 audio /ɪkˈskɝː.ʒən/ uk Your browser doesn't support HTML5 audio /ɪkˈskɜː.ʃən/ Add to word list Add to word list a short trip usually made for pleasure, often by a group of people: excursion to This year's annual excursion will be to Palm Springs.go on an excursion Next week we're going on an excursion. Synonyms expedition jaunt journey (TRIP) junket disapproving outing trip (TRAVEL) excursion into something a short involvement in a new activity: A teacher by profession, this is her first excursion into writing. See more Journeys adventure break-journey carpool carpooling carsick circumnavigation commuting expedition field trip grand tour haul hitch jolly journey peregrination ride traveled traveling trip whistle stop See more results » (Definition of excursion from the Cambridge Advanced Learner's Dictionary & Thesaurus © Cambridge University Press) excursion | Intermediate English excursionnoun [ C ] us Your browser doesn't support HTML5 audio /ɪkˈskɜr·ʒən/ Add to word list Add to word list a short trip usually made for pleasure, often by a group of people: My class is going on an excursion to Niagara Falls. (Definition of excursion from the Cambridge Academic Content Dictionary © Cambridge University Press) Examples of excursion excursion But they rise to the surface at night, and one of them may have encountered our poor shark during such an excursion. From National Geographic Those are monthly excursions to places he used to live in better times. From NPR And he survived a horrible excursion that almost no one survived, and that's where that leathery name came from. From NPR There were no excursions offered beyond the secured area, she said. From CNN Their seemingly-cultural onshore excursions are a product of the more than half a billion dollars their cruise line pays on advertising each year. From Huffington Post Most of all, it's an exciting illustration of the momentum this excursion has generated in such a short period of time. From The Denver Post Depending on how many vessels queue up, the excursion can take hours. From OregonLive.com In fact, if you have a friend who's an experienced rider, bring him or her along for any shopping excursions. From TIME Marathon trainings and other sporting excursions take away from family time, but are hard to give up. From CNN These excursions were always a reminder of what a small and fragile place the city was and is. From The New Yorker He walked to the ceremony in what would be his last excursion out of his home, his sister said. From New York Daily News Although the day before had been cloudy, the skies were bright blue during our excursion. From The Seattle Times Remember that excursions look different in different parts of the word. From ABC News So to enhance each port visit (as well as to increase their profits), cruise lines offer organized shore excursions on all ships for additional fees. From ABC News Road trip season might be winding down (game-day excursions excluded) but that doesn't mean you can't keep dreaming about adventure.
